classificationDefinitions.V1_BLOCKER: A specific compatibility or user-safety condition that prevents responsible stable-interface commitments.
classificationDefinitions.ACCEPTABLE_V1_LIMITATION: A bounded product limitation that can coexist with v1 when it remains explicit and fail-closed.
classificationDefinitions.DOCUMENTATION_GAP: Implemented behavior or scope is not documented precisely enough for stable use.
classificationDefinitions.MEASUREMENT_GAP: The available evidence is honest but insufficient for a broader empirical claim.

items.rationale: UNKNOWN is a first-class non-secure proof result with evidence gaps and is never collapsed into a clean result. Incomplete knowledge is expected in bounded static analysis; preserving it is the user-safety property.
Traversal, parser, identity and dataflow bounds surface TRUNCATED/PARTIAL instead of silently claiming complete analysis. The bound is acceptable because it fails honestly.

The product supports declared literal/direct ESM Express and narrow Python/FastAPI/Flask patterns; CommonJS indirection, dependency injection, callbacks, dynamic construction and most cross-file Python propagation remain unsupported. v1 need not mean universal framework coverage.

items.topic: Repository, parser, identity and dataflow resource bounds
items.rationale: File size/count/depth, AST, identity iteration/fact and dataflow state/edge/path limits protect availability and report their effect. Weakening these bounds would reduce safety.
The pinned 30-repository corpus has selective adjudication and incomplete ground truth. It supports bounded case evidence, not universal accuracy.
Recall and accuracy remain null because complete ground truth does not exist. A stable release can responsibly omit a recall guarantee.
Three historical false PROVEN_INSECURE results were corrected by rule versions 1.0.1 and remain UNKNOWN in current replays; no unresolved confirmed false-insecure result is recorded.

Exact Node 22.18 and 24.11 hosted install/package gates passed on Windows, Ubuntu and macOS, but interactive agent-host versions and broader filesystem/enterprise policy combinations are not continuously exercised.

Deterministic representative runs exist, but host variance is material and there is no controlled cross-platform SLO or statistically powered regression threshold. No unsupported latency guarantee should be made.
Findings prove only catalogued invariants at explicit evidence anchors. Absence of findings, COMPLETE within an engine, or a successful scan is not whole-program or deployed-runtime proof.
Deterministic inventory targets npm lockfile v2/v3 and does not claim dependency reachability, PyPI support, or SPDX output.
Secret scanning is passive, redacted and lexical; it does not validate credentials or prove deployment. Placeholder/key-purpose ambiguity remains UNKNOWN.

Exactly one narrow HttpOnly false-to-true transformation is SAFE. REVIEW_REQUIRED and ARCHITECTURAL work never autoapplies, and any applied SAFE change requires a full rescan and verification conclusion.

Container verification depends on a trusted Docker runtime, a locally available immutable image, kernel controls and bounded temporary workspace capacity. The local runner is explicitly unsandboxed and opt-in.

items.topic: Sandbox workspace copy and filesystem atomicity
items.rationale: The ephemeral copy is text-only and bounded at 10,000 files/100 MiB; local filesystem atomicity cannot provide a universal guarantee against all concurrent or hostile filesystem behavior.

A mandatory local run returned TIMED_OUT and then left its exact cydetix-verify container in Created state. The immediate remove/absence loop can finish before a killed Docker client has completed daemon-side container creation. A second complete 13-case run passed, but the observed race disproves deterministic cleanup and requires a narrow lifecycle fix plus stress regression coverage.

Persistent exact-runtime configuration, root binding and MCP behavior are tested, but host-specific configuration formats and live UI invocation remain best-effort. The primary compatibility policy does not yet label this boundary clearly for v1.

The package publishes dist and declarations without an exports map. Consumers can deep-import implementation modules, leaving it ambiguous which JavaScript/TypeScript APIs v1 semantic versioning would protect.

The shipped CLI and schemas include mature scan/report/MCP contracts alongside setup/status/auth-graph/diagnostic and host-integration surfaces, but no reviewed public policy identifies stable guarantees versus experimental functionality. A v1 release without this boundary would create accidental compatibility promises.

items.topic: Beta.3 public installation and release documentation
items.rationale: README and integration/limitation pages still direct users to older Alpha versions and state that Beta.3 is unpublished or hosted/live publication evidence is unavailable. Those statements contradict the immutable successful Beta.3 release and can cause unsafe or misleading installation choices.
All 27 IDs and versions are inventoried, but the post-v1 compatibility rule for changes to meaning, severity, proof requirements, anchors and remediation ceilings is not yet published.
SARIF 2.1.0 level, fingerprint, code-flow and SAFE-fix behavior is deterministic, but the stability/additive policy for Cydetix-specific property-bag fields is not stated.

items.topic: Exact-version npx invocation on Windows npm 11
items.rationale: The explicit form `npm exec --package=cydetix@0.6.0-beta.3 -- cydetix` runs the exact package, while shorthand `npx cydetix@0.6.0-beta.3` did not resolve the bin under npm 11.19.1 and could fall through to an older global binary. Exact pinning documentation must use the unambiguous form.

items.topic: Cross-platform hostile and permission edge matrix
items.rationale: The current packed edge audit covers Windows paths with spaces, non-Git, monorepo, malformed, hostile, read-only and denied targets; hosted package gates cover Linux/macOS, but the full hostile/permission edge matrix has not been repeated independently on each hosted OS.

The complete history reachable from the audited release commit passes, and independent all-refs Gitleaks passes. A broader deterministic metadata audit of all locally fetched refs found three post-release Dependabot commits on isolated remote branches whose exact bot identity tuples are not yet recorded in the author-allowance policy. They are not ancestors of Beta.3 or main, but should be reviewed before claiming all public refs satisfy the policy.
